findings.title: One instruction. Two actions.
findings.summary: A stream can execute an agent before the browser receives headers. Losing that connection caused the chat to replay through /chat and perform the marker action twice.
findings.observed: 2 persisted fixture actions from 1 instruction; the browser showed a normal final reply.
findings.proposed_direction: Do not automatically replay an uncertain action. Keep fallback only where it is known safe.
findings.evidence_level: real browser + loopback HTTP + unchanged kernel + synthetic upstream and marker agent

findings.title: The old login answers last.
findings.summary: A delayed OAuth result from the old login committed the old synthetic account and cleared the new flow after an account switch.
findings.observed: Old synthetic account committed; new login flow lost in a controlled interleaving.
findings.proposed_direction: A login result may commit only to the flow that issued it.
findings.evidence_level: offline runtime + actual Flask account-switch route + deterministic thread barrier

findings.title: New bytes. Old agent.
findings.summary: A digest-verified, equal-sized edit inside one timestamp second put v2 on disk, but the loader executed cached v1 bytecode.
findings.observed: Disk: v2. Executed: v1. A later timestamp returned v2.
findings.proposed_direction: Execute the accepted source bytes while preserving fresh module, class, and instance state.
findings.evidence_level: offline runtime + actual import route + digest and timestamp controls

system_text: The response stream was interrupted after processing began. It was not retried automatically, to avoid repeating any agent actions. The model's response was interrupted before it finished. Try again.

axis_reasons.consequence: A standard-library agent fails ordinary discovery; this is a real compatibility failure, though narrower than action duplication or account corruption.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: A conventional compatibility repair is the appropriate amount of invention.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: The dataclass control and temporary-registration outcome isolate a useful repair direction without overstating its coverage.
axis_reasons.elegance: Uses Python's existing module mechanism rather than adding a parallel loader; cleanup semantics remain consequential.
axis_reasons.restraint: Scoped registration preserves fresh execution and avoids permanent module accumulation, but the intended module lifetime needs clarification.

proposals.rationale: The archive establishes an eligible proposal, not a release-verified fix. A thoughtful maintainer's main disagreement is whether execution-scoped registration fulfills the intended single-file-agent contract or merely fixes its import-time symptom.
proposals.uncertainty: Runtime reflection, get_type_hints and pickling remain outside the demonstrated control. The strongest counterargument is that immediate removal may leave an apparently repaired agent with unsupported later behavior; retaining modules indefinitely is not automatically a better answer.

axis_reasons.consequence: Account switching must not commit an obsolete account or destroy the newer login flow.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: Standard concurrency discipline is better suited here than an inventive authentication redesign.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: A controlled interleaving through the actual switch route exposes a concrete state-ownership failure.
axis_reasons.elegance: Login-generation ownership fits the existing flow, although correctness depends on consistent synchronization across all outcomes.
axis_reasons.restraint: Ownership checks and a serialized commit boundary target the race without expanding authentication features or services.

proposals.rationale: The reproduced ownership violation justifies a bounded trial of generation-bound completion and atomic commitment relative to switching. This assessment credits protecting an ordinary account-selection promise, not the number of checks or any assumed provider acceptance.
proposals.uncertainty: No candidate implementation establishes complete synchronization yet. The strongest counterargument is that a superficial generation check can leave a check-to-commit race or allow stale expiry, denial or slow-down handling to mutate the new flow; those paths belong within the same ownership discipline.

axis_reasons.consequence: Executing an old agent after a source edit violates the engine's ordinary hotload promise, despite fresh objects.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: A direct source-freshness correction is appropriate; no novel loading architecture is needed.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: Separating fresh identity from fresh executable content makes the failure and correction unusually clear.
axis_reasons.elegance: Source compilation into the existing fresh namespace is coherent, provided metadata, shims and dependency retries remain intact.
axis_reasons.restraint: Bypassing timestamp-and-size bytecode validation is bounded, but unconditional compilation has an unmeasured recurring cost.

proposals.rationale: The discriminating same-size, same-second reproduction supports a trial that stops trusting insufficient bytecode freshness metadata. This and proposal-e address the same defect and should be considered alternative repair framings, not two independent fixes or discoveries.
proposals.uncertainty: The proposed execution path has not been validated as a patch, and realistic sweep cost is unknown. The strongest counterargument is that compiling every agent on every sweep may spend unnecessary CPU; any alternative must still preserve exact source freshness and fresh runtime state.

axis_reasons.consequence: One instruction must not silently become two potentially consequential actions because its reply was lost.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: A small policy reframing supplies the needed insight without unnecessary invention.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: The concrete duplicate action exposes the important distinction between an unknown outcome and a request known not to have run.
axis_reasons.elegance: Replay permission follows evidence of safety rather than header arrival, using the existing communication paths.
axis_reasons.restraint: A client fallback-policy correction preserves known-safe compatibility paths without adding protocol machinery or services.

proposals.rationale: The browser reproduction supports a particularly well-fitted next trial: stop automatic replay after an ambiguous failure while retaining demonstrated safe fallback. These are provisional proposal ratings, not release approval; the declared preference against duplicated side effects favors this judgement.
proposals.uncertainty: The archive does not establish a patched policy or behavior for every transport failure. The strongest counterargument is reduced automatic recovery when a request truly never arrived: users may receive no answer and face an uncertain outcome. That availability tradeoff is real, but silence does not justify replaying a possibly completed action.

axis_reasons.consequence: An accepted agent update should execute its new content rather than silently retain the previous implementation.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: Choosing the simplest measured freshness mechanism is appropriate; redesigning uploads or caching live modules would not be.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: The distinction between verified disk content and executed content identifies the real broken promise without establishing a new discovery.
axis_reasons.elegance: Exact-source execution can fit the existing loader; content-validated code caching would need to justify its additional machinery.
axis_reasons.restraint: The proposal protects fresh runtime state and asks for cost measurement, but leaves the final execution or code-cache mechanism unresolved.

proposals.rationale: The actual import-route evidence makes this eligible for a bounded execution-freshness trial. Its upload-integrity framing does not earn extra taste points over proposal-c: both concern the same stale-code mechanism, and neither establishes historical novelty.
proposals.uncertainty: The final implementation and its cost remain unverified. The strongest counterargument is that digest-oriented framing could encourage unnecessary hashing or caching machinery where direct compilation suffices. The evidence shows stale execution despite correct on-disk bytes, not failure of SHA-256 verification or an established security-boundary bypass.

axis_reasons.consequence: Ordinary single-file agents failing to load breaks a dependable workflow, though the shown case is relatively narrow.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: A small, conventional correction is appropriate for this compatibility problem.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: The direct loader reproduction and controls make the diagnosis credible; the repair itself is not yet verified.
axis_reasons.elegance: Uses the module execution model already in place rather than adding a separate loading path.
axis_reasons.restraint: Scoped registration and cleanup target the demonstrated failure while preserving fresh loads.

proposals.rationale: The dataclass failure is reproduced, and the temporary-registration control supports a focused repair direction. It merits a trial discussion for ordinary hotloading, not a claim that reflection or other module behaviors are covered.
proposals.uncertainty: Runtime get_type_hints, pickling, and later reflection were not tested; the repair direction has not been release-verified. The main counterargument is that the demonstrated case may not represent common agent usage.

axis_reasons.consequence: An old login committing over a newer account-switch flow violates a consequential account ownership promise.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: Concurrency ownership is a relevant repair, with little need for novelty beyond applying it completely.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: A controlled pause/resume on the actual route demonstrates a concrete race and its effects.
axis_reasons.elegance: The ownership rule fits the flow, but must be consistently applied across several completion outcomes.
axis_reasons.restraint: Generation ownership and serialized commit target the race without adding endpoints or another service.

proposals.rationale: The actual account-switch route and deterministic barrier reproduce an important race, making this a credible candidate for a bounded trial. The repair must protect the whole login lifecycle, not only successful responses.
proposals.uncertainty: Only synthetic accounts and side effects were involved, and the repair is not verified. The strongest counterargument is implementation subtlety: expiry, slow-down, and denial paths could still affect a newer flow.

axis_reasons.consequence: A source edit not appearing on the next sweep breaks the stated hotload promise.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: A direct source-loading correction fits; novelty is not needed.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: Same-size, same-second reproduction with fresh-object checks is persuasive, but the stale-bytecode mechanism has related prior art.
axis_reasons.elegance: The loader path is clear, though it must preserve metadata, shims, and dependency retry behavior.
axis_reasons.restraint: Reading and compiling source is a focused remedy, but its recurring cost and compatibility surface need measurement.

proposals.rationale: The same-second reproduction and next-second control isolate stale code from class or instance freshness. The repair direction addresses the general discovery-sweep promise, but should be assessed alongside proposal E because they substantially overlap.
proposals.uncertainty: Realistic agent-count CPU cost and compatibility with loader behavior are unmeasured; no repair is release-verified. The counterargument is that proposal E states the accepted-upload invariant more directly and may be the better framing for the same underlying issue.

axis_reasons.consequence: Replaying after an uncertain response can duplicate an agent action, directly violating a safety-relevant chat promise.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: This is appropriately conservative: avoid unsafe replay rather than invent a new protocol or service.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: The Edge/HTTP fixture demonstrates duplicate actions and contrasts them with 404, accepted-error, and normal controls.
axis_reasons.elegance: The distinction between known-safe replay and uncertain completion is a coherent policy using the existing client flow.
axis_reasons.restraint: Client-side replay classification can address the risk while preserving known-safe fallback paths.

proposals.rationale: The reproduced duplicate action is consequential, and the controls identify the uncertain-header fallback as the meaningful distinction. A narrowly scoped client-policy trial is justified, preserving definitive 404 and unsupported-client fallback behavior.
proposals.uncertainty: The evidence uses a fixture action and loopback HTTP; no repair or live-provider behavior is verified. The key counterargument is that classifying uncertain responses must not accidentally suppress legitimate fallback or obscure an action that actually completed.

axis_reasons.consequence: After a verified upload, executing older source breaks the accepted-bytes contract.
axis_reasons.creativity_fit: The appropriate contribution is enforcing byte identity, not adding a novel subsystem.
axis_reasons.earned_impressiveness: Digest verification, same-size/same-second controls, and namespace checks provide concrete support, but related stale-bytecode work exists.
axis_reasons.elegance: Exact accepted bytes and fresh namespaces express a simple contract within the existing hotload path.
axis_reasons.restraint: It states a focused invariant and leaves implementation choice open, though source execution or code caching must preserve freshness.

proposals.rationale: The verified-upload framing makes the required behavior especially clear, and the controls show that stale execution is distinct from namespace freshness. It deserves discussion as a focused trial, considered together with proposal C rather than as an unrelated fix.
proposals.uncertainty: The evidence does not establish which implementation is smallest or its cost, and the repair is not release-verified. The counterargument is overlap with proposal C: maintainers should avoid treating the same stale-bytecode issue as two independent wins.
